answer: Here is one mechanism that works: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because horizon only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, glacier is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any spiral approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
